newsitem.title: FRANCE: SGS-Thomson says head clean in Italian funds probe.
newsitem.headline: SGS-Thomson says head clean in Italian funds probe.

text.p: European semiconductor group SGS-Thomson Microelectronics NV on Monday rallied behind its executive chairman Pasquale Pistorio who has been named by Italian magistrates in a funds probe.

The company said in a statement that, as it had indicated at the start of the judicial inquiry in May 1995, "the relations between SGS-Thomson and the Corimme consortium have always been based on transparency and total financial rigour."

"The management of the Corimme programmes has been exercised in strict conformity with research programmes approved by the authorities and the accounting practices used have always been very rigourous and responsible," spokesman Carlo Ottaviani said.
The company said it remained at the disposal of the Italian legal authorities to help with their inquiries.
Corimme is a consortium comprising the University of Catania and SGS-Thomson. Catania, in Sicily, is the site of a large semiconductor factory end research centre.

Earlier on Monday the company said magistrates were investigating whether Pistorio misused funds allocated for research. Pistorio was one of 11 people being investigated over allegations the company used government funds earmarked for research for its own business.
The probe adds to further woes in Italy over research funds for the company.
Earlier this month the European Commission was divided, and could not approve, an Italian proposal to give research aid of 18 million Ecu's to SGS-Thomson.

At a news conference on the first half results last week, Pistorio said the aid had been requested under existing research and development rules several years ago. He added that the company had since spent the money itself without waiting for the state aid.
